title: Direction Is Computed Branch by Branch

scenes.tts: A ganglion cell in a rabbit retina fires hard when a spot moves one way across its field. It hardly fires when the spot moves the other way. The first way is its preferred direction. The opposite way is the null direction. Where in the retina is that difference computed, and by which cells?
scenes.visual: Spot sweeps a receptive field; spike rows fill for preferred, nearly empty for null; then a question box.
scenes.narration: A ganglion cell in a rabbit retina fires hard when a spot moves one way across its field. It hardly fires when the spot moves the other way. The first way is its preferred direction. The opposite way is the null direction. Where in the retina is that difference computed, and by which cells?

scenes.tts: Barlow and Levick recorded from such cells in the living rabbit. They flashed two neighbouring places in one receptive field, one after the other. In the preferred order, the pair gave about the sum of the two single responses. In the null order, it gave far fewer spikes than that sum. They inferred that small subunits suppress sequences running the null way. They were tentative about which cells do this.
scenes.visual: Two flash spots in a field; bars for each alone, their sum, and the pair in each order.

scenes.tts: Later work turned to the starburst amacrine cell. Its dendrites radiate from the cell body like the spokes of a wheel. Euler, Detwiler and Denk imaged calcium in single dendrites of ON starburst cells in isolated rabbit retina. A dendrite gave larger calcium signals to motion outward from the cell body than inward. The voltage at the cell body did not show that preference.
scenes.visual: Starburst cell grows; a spot moves out and in along one dendrite; calcium bars; soma voltage chip.

scenes.tts: So each branch has its own preferred direction, set by where the branch points. Briggman, Helmstaedter and Denk then tested the wiring in mouse retina. They imaged each ganglion cell's preferred direction, then reconstructed the same tissue by electron microscopy. Most starburst input came from branches pointing roughly along the ganglion cell's null direction. Branch direction predicted connection better than the line between cell bodies.
scenes.visual: Branch arrows on the starburst cell; then a ganglion cell with preferred and null arrows and starburst branches contacting it from the null-pointing side.
scenes.narration: So each branch has its own preferred direction, set by where the branch points. Briggman, Helmstaedter and Denk then tested the wiring in mouse retina. Most starburst input came from branches pointing roughly along the ganglion cell's null direction. Branch direction predicted connection better than the line between cell bodies.

scenes.tts: How does that asymmetry arise? Pruning would delete the preferred side connections. Wei, Feller and colleagues recorded pairs of starburst and ganglion cells in developing mouse retina. At postnatal days four and seven, inhibition was similar from both sides. Later, inhibition from the null side grew. Inhibition from the preferred side stayed about the same, and those connections were still there in adults.

scenes.tts: Removing the whole starburst population from adult mice abolished direction selectivity in the ganglion cells. That shows the cells are needed in that assay. It does not say whether acetylcholine or GABA carries the asymmetry. So keep this rule. Direction is computed branch by branch, and inhibition strengthens on the null side.
